newsitem.title: UK: ASDA up in strong food retail sector.
newsitem.headline: ASDA up in strong food retail sector.

text.p: Shares in ASDA Group Plc led a sharp rise in UK food retailer stocks on Tuesday amid talk of a buoyant Christmas and hopes for reduced price pressures through 1997, traders said.
Some said investors were looking ahead to trading news next week from J. Sainsbury and Somerfield, also boosted today by a repeated "buy" recommendation from NatWest Securities, market sources said.
"The whole sector is alight," said one market-maker.

Tesco was up 11p at 365 by 0956 GMT, Sainsbury was up 9p at 399-1/2, Safeway Plc was up 13-1/2p to 426-1/2 and ASDA Group Plc -- the most active stock in the UK market with volume of 7.2 million shares -- rose 4p to 128-1/2.
"All the defensive stocks have been doing well recently and money is pouring into this sector," said another trader.

Dealers said there was no specific factor behind today's gains but said domestic stocks not exposed to sterling's strength and benefiting from lower import prices were in favour as international stocks wilt amid earnings downgrades.
And with trading statements due next week, some said there was talk that food retailers may have benefited even as Christmas statements from general retailers provided scant positive surprises.
"There is just a general feeling that the food retailers had a better trading period over Christmas than the general retailers," said one.
"With the colder weather people have been stocking up and pricing pressures have not been at the same level as they were six months ago."
-- David Holmes and Andrew Marshall, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
